judge_assessment.explanation: The worksheet is mathematically exact and I re-derived every item: 7^0=1; 5^-2=1/25; (2/3)^-2=9/4; 3x^-2=3/x^2; x^5*x^-8=x^-3=1/x^3; 2^-3=1/8 > 3^-2=1/9; 4.5e-3=0.0045; (x^-2)^3*x^4=x^-2=1/x^2; 2x^-3/y^-2=2y^2/x^3; 5^-1<5^0<5^1; 4^-2=1/16; and 3x^-2y^4/(6x^3y^-1)=y^5/(2x^5). The judge's structural findings also check out - twelve problems, a real ramp, and every algebraic answer written with positive exponents. Two corrections. First, the judge's own evidence list is inaccurate: its fifth verified value is 'x^2', but problem 5 is x^5 * x^-8 and both answer_key.tex line 59 and the Quick Answers bank print 1/x^3. No problem on this sheet has x^2 as its answer (problem 8's is 1/x^2). The verdict is unaffected, but that entry does not correspond to the artifact. Second, two defects the judge did not reach. The Quick Answers bank prints '6. -' for the comparison 2^-3 versus 3^-2, which gate_log.txt records as PASS and which answer_key.tex boxes as '1/8 > 1/9' - the bank's only blank row is the one comparison on the sheet, and the sheet has no manual items for the glyph to legitimately mean. And problem 11 asks the student to 'Explain in one sentence what Dana did wrong, then write the correct value as a fraction'; verify.json id 11 is a single eval (1/16) with a declared trap of -16, and there is no manual entry anywhere in the file, so the explanation half of an error-analysis item is recorded as machine-verified.

strengths_to_preserve: The set covers five genuinely different question shapes rather than twelve of the same: evaluate (1, 2, 3), rewrite with positive exponents (4, 9), apply a named law (5, 8, 12), compare and order (6, 10), scientific notation (7) and error analysis (11). Problem 3 in particular - (2/3)^-2 = 9/4 - makes the reciprocal idea visible as a flip rather than a rule to memorise.

Problem 6 is chosen so that the intuitive shortcut fails: comparing the exponents (-3 versus -2) gives the wrong order, and only comparing the values 1/8 and 1/9 gives the right one. The key states the reason in one line ('the larger reciprocal has the smaller denominator'), which is the actual content of the comparison.

The directions state the misconception before the student can form it - 'A negative exponent never makes a value negative. It means reciprocal' - and problem 11 then plants exactly that error (Dana's -16) with the wrong value declared as machine-checked trap data in verify.json rather than typed into the stem by hand.

Problem 9 (2x^-3 / y^-2) is the one item where a negative exponent has to move UP from the denominator, and it is placed after the two easier rewrite items so the direction of travel is the new thing being tested rather than the notation.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt cannot render a relation: it sympifies the string expected, sympify('>') raises, and the fallback prints '---', the glyph the module reserves for manual-only ids. On this sheet that blanks the single comparison row while the worked solution two pages later boxes it correctly.
evidence: verify.json id 6: {type: compare, values: ['2**(-3)', '3**(-2)'], order: relation, expected: '>'}, recorded PASS in gate_log.txt.
answer_key.tex line 70 boxes '1/8 > 1/9' for the same problem.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 57-61 - the str branch's except clause returns '---'.

root_causes.description: An explanation attached to a numeric answer is treated as covered by that answer. Problem 11 is an error-analysis item whose first requested output is a diagnosis in words, and it is declared as a bare eval with no manual entry, so the run reports zero items needing review on a sheet that contains a find-and-fix problem.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 11: 'Dana was asked to evaluate 4^-2 and wrote -16. Explain in one sentence what Dana did wrong, then write the correct value as a fraction.'
verify.json id 11 is a single eval entry (a**(-2) at a=4 -> 1/16) plus a trap; the file has no manual entry.
machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags = false; gate_log.txt reports 'BUILD PASSED - all gates green'.
SKILL.md line 257 already states the rule this violates: 'Use manual for: ... any explanation/reasoning answer.'

improvements.title: Print '1/8 > 1/9' in the bank instead of the manual em-dash for problem 6
improvements.proposed_change: Special-case relation strings in render_quick_answers._fmt ahead of the sympify call: for expected in {'<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!='}, emit the operator between the entry's compared values so id 6 renders as '2^-3 > 3^-2'. Keep '---' strictly for ids whose entries are all manual.
improvements.regression_test: Render this task's verify.json and assert row 6 contains a relation operator rather than '---'. The assertion fails against the shipped answer_key.pdf, which prints '6. -', and passes after the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The only blank row in an otherwise complete twelve-row bank is filled, and the bank stops contradicting the boxed answer in the same document.
improvements.risk: Minimal here - one short row; the general risk is width, which column_count already handles.

improvements.title: Require a manual entry for problem 11's 'explain what Dana did wrong'
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate step that scans each worksheet problem block for open-response imperatives and fails the build unless that id carries a manual entry, so problem 11 declares both the eval (1/16) and a manual entry for the diagnosis. Make SKILL.md's existing prose rule enforceable by saying explicitly that an error-analysis item's naming-the-error half is always manual even when its numeric half is verified.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with problem 11's stem and a verify.json id 11 holding only the eval entry. The check must exit non-zero naming the explanation slot; adding {id: 11, type: manual, desc: 'names the negate-versus-reciprocate confusion'} makes it pass and moves the run exit code from 0 to 2.
improvements.expected_impact: The diagnosis half of the sheet's only misconception item reaches a human reviewer instead of being reported as fully machine-verified.
improvements.risk: One extra manual item per sheet of this shape; verb matching must be scoped to the problem body to avoid firing on the directions block, which here says 'Show the law you used ... before you simplify'.

case_summary: A clean, mathematically exact zero-and-negative-exponent fluency sheet - I checked all twelve answers independently and every one is right, with positive-exponent form respected throughout - and a well-varied ramp across evaluation, rewriting, laws, comparison, scientific notation and error analysis. Problem 6 is the standout: it is built so that comparing exponents gives the wrong answer and only comparing values gives the right one. Two defects remain after the ACCEPT. The Quick Answers bank prints '6. -' for that same comparison, which the gate log records as PASS and the key boxes as 1/8 > 1/9, because _fmt sympifies the string '>' and falls back to the manual glyph. And problem 11's 'explain in one sentence what Dana did wrong' is declared as a bare eval with no manual entry, so the sheet reports nothing for review even though it ends with a find-and-fix item. Separately, the judge's evidence list cites a verified 'x^2' that no problem on this sheet has; problem 5's answer is 1/x^3 in both the key and the bank.
